The player used the movement technique 'Shenwai' once 3. The player used Wandering Wight (幽魂) Spirit (精魄) twice 4. The player drank wine twice to restore health

db_evidence.notes: The question's own total_intervals/clue_interval [17074, 17238] does NOT contain the Xiao Lilong fight. Querying episodes 30sec rows in that window (memcli sql, day timeline, 16900-17400) shows a completely different Black Myth: Wukong boss fight against an unnamed 'large mossy, antlered enemy' / 'hulking boss', ending in a defeat notice around 17220-17250 -- no mention of Xiao Lilong, immobilize 定身术, 身外身法, 幽魂, or wine-drinking anywhere in that text. By contrast, episodes rows at 52170-52710 (queried directly) explicitly name '小黄龙' (Xiao Huanglong/Xiao Lilong) at 52200-52230 and end with the on-screen text '已击败 妖王·小黄龙' ('defeated Demon King Xiao Huanglong') at 52650-52680 -- this is unambiguously the correct fight referenced by the question. All 5 rollouts independently retrieved this same 52200-52680 window via semantic_search/run_sql, so retrieval itself worked correctly; the question metadata's clue_interval/total_intervals field is mislabeled/wrong for this item. The specific skill-activation counts (definitely for wine-drinking, and the 1 vs 5 vs 2 activation counts) are not present as structured text in episodes/event_steps at all -- they exist only as visual detail requiring clip_qa, and clip_qa's counts are inconsistent between calls on the identical interval (see rollout 0's two passes: 4/3/5/9 vs 5/1/2/3 for the same four categories).

root_causes: clip_qa (the visual sub-agent) gives materially different activation counts when called multiple times over the identical 52200-52680s interval (demonstrated within rollout 0: immobilize 4->5, spirit 5->2, wine 9->3), so whichever pass the agent trusts last determines the final answer and none of the 5 rollouts' final counts matched the reference exactly

This is a Hallucination Detection question with two true and two false claims; agents that got individual counts close to correct (rollout 4: 5/1/2/2, matching statements 2 and 4) still failed because they mechanically confirmed all four statements as true rather than recognizing 1 and 3 as the injected false claims to be rejected
Rollout 3 submitted after only a single clip_qa call with no cross-check, compounding a single noisy count into the worst answer (score 0)

The question's clue_interval/total_intervals metadata field points to the wrong 164-second window (17074-17238, an unrelated Black Myth: Wukong fight) rather than the actual Xiao Lilong fight at 52200-52680; this did not directly hurt any rollout since all 5 found the right window via semantic search on entity name and boss description, but it means this leaf's own total_intervals/clue_interval field (copied from the question file) should not be trusted as the ground-truth location
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly localized the Xiao Lilong boss fight to 52200-52680 via semantic_search on entity/episode text and run_sql filtering by time window, despite the question metadata pointing elsewhere
Rollouts that split the interval into sub-segments for clip_qa (1, 2, 4) generally produced counts closer to the reference than the single whole-interval pass in rollout 3
Shenwai (once) and the general presence of wine-drinking and spirit-summoning were reliably detected as occurring at all, even when exact counts were wrong
transferable_lessons: For fine-grained visual counting questions (exact activation counts of a skill/action across several minutes of footage), a single clip_qa call is unreliable -- but even multiple calls over the identical footage do not converge, so the agent should not treat any single clip_qa count as ground truth without cross-checking via a second independent pass and reconciling discrepancies rather than blindly taking the latest number

For Hallucination Detection question types with N candidate statements, after gathering per-statement evidence the agent should explicitly ask 'which of these are the injected false claims' rather than defaulting to affirming every statement whose count happens to match

When the question's own clue_interval/total_intervals metadata does not match content matching the question's entities (e.g. a named boss like Xiao Lilong absent from that window), retrieval should be driven by entity/keyword search across the full timeline rather than trusting the metadata window, and evaluators reading temporal_certificate/total_intervals for this item should recompute the true window from the DB rather than trusting the stored clue_interval

Splitting a long combat interval into 2-3 sub-windows for clip_qa counting tends to produce more accurate per-category counts than one pass over the whole interval, but still is not reliable enough for exact-count claims without additional verification passes
open_questions: Whether the reference answer '2, 4' was itself scored against ground truth generated from a human/automated review of the 52200-52680 footage, or against the (wrong) 17074-17238 window -- if the latter, the reference answer's correctness for the ACTUAL Xiao Lilong fight content is unverified by this analysis (we only confirmed retrieval location, not that the true counts in the 52200-52680 fight are exactly immobilize!=5, shenwai=1, spirit!=2, wine=2)

Why the question's clue_interval/total_intervals field points to an unrelated Black Myth: Wukong boss fight window instead of the Xiao Lilong fight -- this looks like a metadata/labeling bug in question generation rather than anything the agent could have avoided
